name: c-portrait-straight-to-camera
prompt: A tall upright sheet of warm ivory paper carrying one figure drawn in black ink with a fine pen: a stout, well-fed gentleman of about 1919, invented for this picture and resembling no real person, seated squarely at the centre of a plain slatted park bench and facing us dead on, the eye level of the drawing at his chest so we see him whole from polished spats to the crown of a tall glossy silk hat. He leans back at ease, thighs spread to make room for a round belly buttoned into a tight double-breasted waistcoat with a watch chain looped across it, a long dark tailcoat open at the front, a cane propped against one knee with his gloved hand folded over its knob. Fleshy chins, neat waxed moustache, small hooded eyes fixed on ours, mouth turned up at one corner in a quiet, contented smile, as if he has just been proved right again. The seat on his right is bare except for a wooden crutch fallen flat across the slats; the seat on his left is bare except for a modern hospital pass on its cord, slipped half over the edge, its card blank. No park around him: no trees, lamps or path, just the empty paper, one short horizontal stroke for the ground and a little hatched shadow pooled under the bench. Flat, shadowless, frontal light like a costume study, so every button and fold reads plainly. All shading is built from line alone: dense cross-hatching in the coat and hat, finer single-direction strokes on the trousers, a few dots of stipple on the cheeks, the face kept mostly open. Ink black on ivory only, no colour, no wash, no grey tones. The upper third of the sheet, above the hat, is left as clean empty paper with nothing drawn in it; no words, letters, numbers, signature or speech balloon on the sheet at all. Thanks.
